reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the first three premises by stating that dislocation barriers pin domain walls, that small precipitates below the domain wall thickness do not deteriorate coercivity, and that coherent precipitates cause only modest pinning. However, the fourth premise—that larger, less coherent precipitates will increase coercivity—is not supported by E1; it is an extrapolation from the opposite case (small, coherent precipitates) and lacks direct prior evidence in the cited passage.
premises: Microstructure features that impede dislocations also pin magnetic domain walls, increasing coercivity.
Nanoprecipitates smaller than the domain wall thickness do not interact with Bloch walls and thus do not increase coercivity.
Coherent precipitates create negligible distortion fields and entail modest domain wall pinning.
Larger, less coherent precipitates generate increased local strain fields and interfacial disturbances that pin domain walls more effectively.
